description: A 3040-byte crafted MKV containing a 128x128 gbrp HEVC stream, when processed through FFmpeg's boxblur filter with radius expression `min(w,h)/2`, triggers a 1-byte out-of-bounds heap read in `blur8` at libavfilter/vf_boxblur.c:157. The overflow occurs during vertical blur processing via the call chain vblur → blur_power → blur → blur8, reading past a 16448-byte heap allocation. The bug is deterministic: three independent runs in a fresh container produced identical ASAN reports. An attacker who can supply input to an FFmpeg pipeline using boxblur can at minimum cause a crash (DoS) and potentially leak adjacent heap memory.
reproduction: 1. Craft a 128x128 gbrp HEVC stream muxed into MKV (PoC is 3040 bytes)
2. Have the target run: ffmpeg -i poc.mkv -vf "boxblur=min(w\,h)/2" -frames:v 1 -f null -
3. During vblur → blur_power → blur → blur8, a 1-byte OOB heap read occurs and ASAN aborts
technical_details: ASAN: READ of size 1 past the end of a 16448-byte heap region in blur8 (vf_boxblur.c:157). During the vertical blur pass, the blur kernel indexes one byte beyond the allocated plane buffer when the blur radius is derived from `min(w,h)/2` on a 128x128 gbrp frame, indicating a missing or off-by-one bounds check on the source pointer in the inner blur loop.
title: Heap-buffer-overflow in vf_boxblur.c:157
